title: FL-IDS wall-clock testbed: measuring synchronous and asynchronous federated aggregation on real processes
description:
Container-based testbed and complete raw measurements behind the paper Measuring on the Critical Path Inverts the Answer: A Real-Testbed Study of Synchronous and Asynchronous Federated Learning for Intrusion Detection.

The testbed runs a real aggregator and real client processes as separate containers with cgroup CPU/memory tiers and tc netem network shaping, and measures wall-clock time to a target macro-F1 rather than communication rounds. Four aggregation strategies are implemented: synchronous FedAvg, FedAsync, FedBuff as published, and a staleness-plus-data-size buffered variant, together with an ablation that isolates each ingredient.

The archive contains the raw output of all 2858 runs as per-run configuration and metrics files. This deliberately includes the superseded batches measured with evaluation on the aggregator's critical path, so that the measurement effect reported in the paper, a roughly 14x cost charged to asynchronous rules against 1.6x for the synchronous barrier, can be verified independently rather than taken on trust. A manifest maps each batch to the table or figure it supports.

Datasets (CICIDS2017, Bot-IoT, N-BaIoT) are not redistributed; the exact partitioning and preprocessing code is provided instead.
